still_had_to_guess: What <origin> means: arrive gives the flag as --origin <origin> and no example. help door and the refusal say a scheme and a host.

Which flag was wrong: INVALID_ARGUMENTS says the arguments do not match the usage and points to help. It does not name the missing or extra flag, so door check without its two required numbers costs a second read.

The Entry ID: the blank entry gives the form (date, short lowercase label, three-digit number) and does not say what the number counts or who picks the label. feedback check says only whether the ID is already in this checkout's notebook.
Where an adoption record is found: door rights reads a local file, and nothing at the door says where a host keeps one. Finding or fetching a record was not built.
That --out wants an absolute path: arrive does not say; help feedback and the refusal do.
Whether to send: door plan says the decision is made outside the kit. That is a choice left to the caller, not a gap in the text; the walk did not send.

review_fixes.note: Independent reviewers examined the four commits above and returned 27 findings. Each was reproduced on head_before_record before anything was changed. One line for each finding id follows; the tests named are in the three kit test files and tests/own-door.test.mjs.

findings.C1: fixed. door rights no longer hands the JSON Schema check a record with an array longer than the installed schema allows for any array (1024), and stops the check after 5 seconds. Before, on this machine: 0.3 s at 8,000 rows and 1.2 s at 16,000; the review measured 78 s at 64,000. After: a 1.8 MB file with one array of 600,000 rows read in 0.3 s, and two nested shapes inside the first bound stopped at 5 s.
findings.C2: fixed. assigned_secret reads an environment name, an ini, YAML or JSON key; url_credentials and basic_value are new kinds; four key prefixes and the PGP header were added. 21 planted lines are warned about and none is echoed.
findings.C3: fixed in part. A path is found after * | < > and a comma, and a share path has its own kind. The two harmless lines the review named are still flagged, knowingly: a row is a line to look at.
findings.C4: fixed. The plan for another origin is the first next action. A lifted plan, and a check, say which default rule was set aside and whether an IP literal is in a range the vendored list holds as not globally reachable. The default rule still reads text only, as the plan says under does_not_guard.
findings.C5: fixed. The note speaks for its own section and says a row can still carry host text. Control, format and line-separator characters in host text are printed as \u{HEX} in the short form; --full is untouched.
findings.C6: fixed without changing an exit. finding.also and the exit reason carry a status other than active and an as_of earlier than the review; reviewed_at has a relation word.
findings.refusal-echoes-target: fixed in words and in order. The README, help and the code comment say what holds: userinfo, path, query and fragment are never copied; the origin of a target the flag could admit appears in the suggested plan.
findings.door-check-args-unnamed: fixed. A missing required flag is named (problem.missing), and each of the two numbers has its own reason. An unknown or repeated flag is still not named.
findings.draft-receipt-gap: fixed. A receipt whose result says it is an adoption record is refused with that one step; help and the README say it too.
findings.first-look-rows-and-next: fixed. Checks not sent for want of budget are counted under not_passed.left_out and not listed; next gives the full-check command when a valid manifest was read and the budget was the limit.
findings.rights-origin-mismatch-exit-0: fixed without changing the exit. The exit reason says which way the comparison went, and finding.also carries record_names_another_origin.
findings.rights-finding-word-on-exit-3: fixed. finding.also carries pass_rows_on_expired_evidence; reviewed_at.relation says after_as_of.
findings.help-two-words: fixed. Words after a command name are not read: help door plan answers as help door. A word every object answers to (toString) is no longer taken for a command.
findings.feedback-two-headings: fixed. A level-two heading with a date that does not exist is given as a warning with its line; beside a dated heading the file is exit 4 and no part is read.
findings.exit-0-wording-in-help: fixed. The wording the design had set for exit 0 was changed, because it was true of door and feedback bodies only.
findings.feedback-new-says-hints-twice: fixed. parts no longer repeats what the entry's own comments say: 8,774 bytes before, 7,498 after. route is still printed in full by three commands, as designed.
findings.H1: fixed. One test holds exit 0, 3 and 4 bodies and a plan to a list of words that would bless a service, and looks for each not_established line, the scope and covers.not_more by content. The rights line about safety is pinned.
findings.H4: fixed by addition. The four state words are unchanged; manifest.means is one fixed sentence for each, and not_found says only that the status was not 200.
findings.H5: left open. Nothing in this checkout or its history shows the order of work in tasks 1 to 3, and the author of these fixes did not build them. The not_established line stays.
findings.H6: fixed. The test asks git about .mcp.json at the root as well as .claude/.
findings.H7: fixed. The comment and the README say six of the eight fields are the existing entry's, and that Network vantage and Reply path answer bullets 3 and 7.

final_gate_fixes.note: An independent final check of the review-fix commit returned one major and three minor findings. Each was reproduced on that commit before anything was changed. The tests for the first three were written first and seen failing.

findings.C1-other-check-unbounded: fixed. The other check, run by itself, now has the same time limit as Observe's inspection; when it is stopped, cross_document is not_run, the finding is undetermined with reason no_check_finished, and the exit is 4. The expiry pass reads each expires_at once and orders readings by the rule of compareRfc3339 (a test compares the two on 18 times, every pair). The file that had taken 108 s took 5.3 s; the long-expiry file that had taken 5.9 s took 0.3 s.
findings.time-limit-names-the-wrong-check: fixed. The sentence names what is stopped: Observe's inspection, which runs the JSON Schema check and then the other check; which of the two it was in is not recorded. The other check is then run by itself under the same limit, not without one.
findings.H1-two-changes-still-pass: fixed. checker_result.covers.rule and covers.not_more are compared whole, and for a refused target the flag could admit, the host is counted in stdout: once.
findings.agreed-design-departures: accepted, no change: the reworded exit-0 sentence and the added output keys stay as the review fixes left them. They are listed under review_fixes.changes_to_agreed_shapes.
